title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Direct Deposit Prenote Days on a Payment Election
content:
Prenote days are business days added to the election lead time of a payment election on an Unemployment Benefit Claims record. Their number is read from the claim's payment history.

## Terms

- **A returned deposit** is a cancellation with reason returned by the bank booked on the claim.
- **A direct-deposit payment** is a payment issued on the claim through direct deposit to checking or savings.
- **The returned-deposit window** is the 6 months before the handling date, read by the date the cancellation was booked.

## Prenote days

| Payment history of the claim | Prenote days |
|---|---|
| A deposit on the claim was returned by the bank within the 6 months before the handling date | 5 |
| No deposit so returned, and no direct-deposit payment has ever been issued on the claim | 2 |
| No deposit so returned, and a direct-deposit payment has been issued on the claim | None |

## Hypothetical cases

- A deposit was returned by the bank 2 months before the handling date: 5 prenote days, whatever other payments the claim shows.
- A deposit was returned 8 months before the handling date and the claim has had direct-deposit payments: the return falls outside the 6-month window, so no prenote days apply.
- The claim has only ever been paid on the state benefit debit card and has no returned deposit: 2 prenote days.
